narration: Clean clothes once meant a journey as well as a chore. A woman holds a length of white cloth beside the water. In her other hand is a wooden laundry beater. Wetting, beating, and rinsing called for repeated work. Look at the hand gripping the fabric, then the bend of her back. Others work farther away, making this a shared place rather than a solitary scene. A visitor might connect the white clothing with the effort needed to keep it clean. The pretty riverside can draw our eyes away from that physical effort. The painting is attributed to Uncho. From the TJ Kim Collection, an ordinary task helps us see the people behind a clean garment.
